title: SPARC Cat Acute UroMOCA Implantation Surgery
author: Brett Hanzlicek
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf2pjqdn
materials: Replace the bladder in its orthotopic postion.

steps.title: Prepare Cat for Surgery
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the cat, shave the abdomen, and attach the animal to monitors.

steps.title: Sterilize Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Drape the cat and perform a betadine scrub on the abdomen and genitals.

steps.title: Insert Bladder Catheter
steps.instruction: Insert a 3.5Fr catheter into the bladder through the urethra using surgilube.

substeps.instruction: Retract the foreskin and advance the catheter directly into the center of the triangular shaped glans.
Advance the catheter until resistance is met, then pull back 2-3 cm.

steps.title: Plan and Make Skin Incision
steps.instruction: Mark a midline 3-4 cm line based on imaging results to locate the bladder, then make the incision.

substeps.instruction: Make the incision through the skin using a #15 blade.
Cut through the fat (separating it from the external fascia).
Bluntly dissect the skin off the muscle.
Use a Weitlaner retractor to keep the incision open.

steps.title: Enter the Abdominal Cavity
steps.instruction: Create an opening in the midline muscle to access the abdomen.

substeps.instruction: Make a small incision in the midline muscle using a scalpel or scissors, ensuring not to go through completely.
Use a right angle or small hemostat to enter the abdomen bluntly and open the muscle/fascia to the length of the incision.
Replace the retractor to incorporate the abdominal musculature or use two fingers to spread the abdomen open to visualize the bladder.

steps.title: Deliver the Bladder
steps.instruction: Extract the bladder from the incision for external manipulation.

substeps.instruction: Optionally remove some fluid from the bladder to decrease the required incision length.
Grasp the bladder with a blunt pick-up and deliver it out of the incision.
Place the bladder on several wet pieces of gauze to avoid contact with fur or instruments.

steps.title: Prepare Bladder for Incision
steps.instruction: Mark the incision site and secure the bladder dome.

substeps.instruction: Identify an area on the dome that is less vascular and not covered in fat (avoiding the ureters which enter dorsally near the bladder neck).
Mark a 1 cm line on the dome of the distended bladder using a skin marker.
Place a 4-0 vicryl full thickness stay-suture at each apex of the planned incision and keep them untied in a hemostat.

steps.title: Perform Cystotomy
steps.instruction: Open the bladder to allow for device placement.

substeps.instruction: Incise the bladder using a #10 blade.
Quickly place a closed hemostat or pickup inside the lumen to maintain the opening.
Use tissue scissors to open the rest of the mucosa (the full 1 cm may not be necessary due to bladder stretchability).

steps.title: Position for Device Placement
steps.instruction: Prepare the bladder for the device by holding the apical sutures.

substeps.instruction: Hold one apical suture while an assistant holds the other suture.

steps.title: Close the Cystotomy
steps.instruction: Irrigate the bladder with saline and close the incision in layers.

substeps.instruction: Close the mucosa with a running 4-0 vicryl suture, using small bites for a good closure.
Close the muscle with several interrupted 4-0 vicryl sutures.
Tie the initial stay sutures.
Control any detrusor bleeding with manual pressure or a suture.

steps.title: Perform Leak Test
steps.instruction: Perform a quick leak test while visualizing the bladder incision to determine filling limits for post-op cystogram and cystometry.

steps.title: Close Abdominal Wall
steps.instruction: Close the abdominal wall and irrigate the wound.

substeps.instruction: Close the abdominal wall in one layer with 3-0 surgipro running suture.
Optionally place 1-2 interrupted sutures in the middle of the incision for extra support.

steps.title: Close Subcutaneous Layer
steps.instruction: Use leftover vicryl to place a few Scarpa's or subcutaneous fat stitches.

steps.title: Close Skin
steps.instruction: Close the skin with simple, interrupted nylon sutures.

substeps.instruction: Place sutures closely together.
Avoid over-tightening the nylon sutures.
Cut the tails short to prevent irritation or interference by the cat.
